_meta.what: Gold set for FieldVision baseball retrieval: 37 modern-style scouting notes, each labeled with the Branch Rickey reports it should retrieve.
_meta.label_status_note: Notes and labels were drafted by Claude (AI) on 2026-11-12 under the protocol below. No human has audited them yet. Treat every number computed from this file as provisional until Jake or a coach spot-checks the labels.
_meta.notes_note: Every note describes a FICTIONAL player. Each was written from one seed Rickey report, restated in the vocabulary a college scout uses today. They are not real scouting notes.
protocol: 1. Seeds: 45 Rickey documents drawn with random.Random(20261112).sample from the 1,161 documents between 300 and 1,400 characters. No retriever was involved in choosing them.

2. Exclusions: 8 of the 45 were dropped because they are not evaluations of a player's tools (contract and record cards, trade memos, a one-line hitting remark, a team list). 37 seeds remain: 20 pitchers, 17 position players.
3. Note: for each seed, a modern note was written that describes the same profile without the player's name and without copying Rickey's phrasing.

4. Labels: the seed, plus other reports on the same player in the same role that evaluate the tools the note describes and do not contradict its headline trait. Found by surname search and read one by one. Duplicate transcriptions of a labeled page are labeled too.
5. Not labeled: reports on other players, even when the profile is similar. So precision@5 is a lower bound and its ceiling is (number of labeled reports)/5 for most notes.
known_limits: The same author wrote the notes and chose the vocabulary fix under test, so the fix may be flattered.
Labels are incomplete by design (see protocol step 5).
37 notes is small. Differences of a few points are not meaningful.

queries.note:
Tyler Renko
RHP, junior, 6'0 185. Fastball is light, 84-86, and gets hit hard when he leaves it in the zone against good hitters. Has to pitch backwards: changeup and curveball are his outs and he needs to throw them in any count. If he keeps challenging people with the heater he tops out as a midweek arm.

Marcus Dell
RHP, sophomore, 6'2 195. Three-pitch mix and all three are usable: firm fastball, big slow curveball with real depth, and a changeup good enough to keep hitters off the fastball. Doesn't need a fourth pitch. Whole thing comes down to strike throwing; tends to take something off just to get it over. Needs to trust the breaking ball and changeup when behind in the count.

Evan Brandt
LHP, junior, 6'0 175. Strike thrower, fills the zone with a low three-quarter, nearly sidearm fastball that stays at the knees. Curveball has bite but isn't consistent yet. Very coachable: fixed a glove-side tipping habit as soon as it was pointed out. Changeup still a work in progress and he's reluctant to use it in games.

Dee Whitlow
SS, sophomore, 5'10 170. Plus-plus runner, flies down the line. Quick release and soft hands at short, covers a ton of ground. Left-handed bat with a disciplined approach, doesn't chase, tough out, and sneaky pop now and then. Everyday shortstop profile.

Jace Mullen
RHP, freshman. Big arm with plenty of stuff but can't find the zone, constantly behind 2-0 and 3-0. Two-pitch guy right now, fastball and breaking ball, no changeup or won't throw it. Immature on the mound; needs innings and needs to learn how to pitch, not just throw.

Nico Farrell
C, junior, 5'9 165. Small-framed catcher, moves well behind the plate and handles a staff, smart kid. Arm is accurate and good enough, throws with sound mechanics. Contact bat with no real power, but he doesn't strike out. Below-average runner. Everything but the speed plays.

Grant Okafor
RHP, senior. Velocity is gone. Used to be a power arm, now can't throw hard at all and has no feel for the strike zone. Walked four and hit two in 3.1 innings. Only looks like himself when he drops down and throws from underneath, and even that is half of what it was. Hard to watch; arm may be done.

Ray Castellano
UTIL IF, fifth-year senior, right-handed hitter. Tools are all below average: doesn't hit, doesn't run, arm is short. But he's a heady, scrappy, aggressive player who knows every trick in the game. Future is in coaching, not playing; would make a good manager.

Luke Hartsfield
RHP, freshman, 6'5, 20 years old. Fastball is solid, not overpowering. Curveball is adequate. Changeup is the separator, a really good one off the fastball. Slight differences in his delivery from pitch to pitch that can be cleaned up. Three pitches are enough, don't add a fourth. He'll go as far as his command takes him.

Sam Petrovic
RHP, sophomore, 6'0 180. Big-league velocity when he reaches back, but command goes when he overthrows. Curveball is a good one that he throws from two slots, three-quarters and nearly sidearm; needs to be more consistent with it. Changeup has a chance to be a real weapon, spin on it is right. Timeline depends on locating the fastball and curve.

Owen Tash
C, sophomore. Needs daily reps behind the plate. Footwork on his throws is the issue: takes an extra step before releasing, even though the arm is strong enough to throw from the catch. Return throws to the pitcher are erratic, possibly a mental block. Should catch every bullpen just to work on getting the ball back quickly and accurately.

Brock Dennehy
C, junior, short and stocky build. Real raw power in the bat, good setup and swing with no obvious holes, should hit. Long, looping arm action on his throws. Some people question his receiving, but I didn't see a problem that reps won't fix. Word is he rates himself pretty highly.

Tony Varga
3B/IF, sophomore. Not a true third baseman: he can catch it and throw it but that's it; doesn't know how to apply a tag. At least he's swinging the bat now instead of taking strikes. Baserunning is the big problem: short stationary lead, no jump, no feel for getting a break, especially off second base.

Will Kessinger
RHP (converted OF), junior, 6'5. Came in as an outfielder but the bat never developed, so we're trying him on the mound. Fastball is good and he commands it. That's all he has right now: breaking ball isn't there yet and no changeup. Off-the-charts aptitude though, picks up anything you show him right away.

Ben Aldridge
RHP, junior, 170 lbs. Fringy across the board: fastball is only fair, curveball is fair, has a slower version of the curve, just starting to learn a changeup. Strike throwing isn't good enough yet. Nothing here to get excited about. A maybe, nothing more.

Dominic Ruiz
1B/OF, freshman, big strong kid, very young. Swing-and-miss is a major concern: pulls his head off the ball and can't square anything up, will strike out a lot. But you can't write off that size and strength at his age; could look different in two years. Runs okay. Worth following.

Aiden Marsh
SS/UTIL, junior. Solid across the board without a carrying tool: decent bat, decent runner, decent arm. Plays shortstop too shallow and doesn't know how to hold a runner at second. Arm isn't enough to make the play deep in the hole. Versatile, can play anywhere; value is as a utility man.

Cal Brenner
LHP, junior, 21. Left-hander with a deep pitch mix and a real chance to pitch at the next level. Big problem with runners on first: never comes set, would get called for a balk on every pitch.

Mickey Dolan
2B/OF, freshman, 18, 160 lbs, throws right, bats left. Does everything well, nothing spectacular: good runner, good arm, good hitter without power. Smart, aggressive baserunner who makes the most of his speed. Gamer, the kind of player who makes a lineup hard to beat.

Hank Brody
C, junior, 21, big strong right-handed-hitting catcher. Arm didn't show well; the backup threw better. Looked lost at the plate, 0-for with weak at-bats. Doesn't run. Not a draft guy.

Pete Lindqvist
RHP, senior, 6'3 190, Big Ten arm. Fastball is fairly good, not plus. Curveball is fringy. Changeup is too firm to be useful right now, though he could learn one. What he has is makeup: determined, confident, a real competitor with courage. Has a chance but he's raw.

Manny Ortega
OF, sophomore, bats left, throws left, undersized. Pesky hitter who sprays the ball and battles every at-bat, with enough pop to keep outfielders honest. Could be an everyday guy.

Kyle Burdette
3B/IF, junior. Big-league tools. Two knocks: always nursing some injury, real or not, and he won't get in front of hard-hit ground balls. Plays them off to the side instead of keeping his body behind the ball.

Trey Lawson
LHP, sophomore, tall. Fastball is good enough to pitch at the next level. Curveball is a true downer and he has a hard and a slow version, but can't command either. Changeup off the fastball might be his best pitch. Concern is the makeup: flat, no energy, no fight, looks like he doesn't care. No obvious mechanical reason for the wildness.

Lamar Givens
C, junior. Receiving is a problem: slow to react on a catchable foul pop, got there late and dropped it. Quick release but arm strength is average. No power; swing and setup are fine but it's not a home run stroke. Grows on you though: tough out, pesky hitter.

Cory Wendt
2B, senior. Came in late at second and looked bad in both at-bats, though the bat is the only tool he has. Zero aggressiveness, doesn't run out ground balls. Average runner at best. Can't play second base; only way he helps is in a corner outfield spot.

Joe Halvorsen
LHP, senior. Veteran left-hander with outstanding command, some of the best spot pitching I've seen. Lives on the outside edge to hitters who stand off the plate, and keeps everything down, maybe three or four pitches above the belt all game. Pitches with a plan.

Ron Strickland
OF/3B, junior, tall, right-handed hitter. Very good arm. Runner is average at best. Swing looks right and there's power in there, but he never hits in games when I see him. Everyone else is high on him. Passive, doesn't take chances in the field or on the bases.

Don Fairley
RHP, junior, 22, tall sidearmer. Good fastball and repeats his delivery, should throw strikes. One-pitch guy, nothing else in the arsenal worth mentioning. Not ready, and unless he comes up with a second effective pitch he won't pitch at the next level.

Lee Sandoval
RHP, senior, 27 (older transfer). Good fastball, not great. Has a curveball, also not great. Best weapon is a slow curve he uses as a change of pace, really messes with timing. Very good command. Slow to the plate with runners on. Fields his position well.

Chuck Novak
1B/RHP, freshman, 18, tall. Two-way guy but the bat is the story: excellent setup and swing, should hit. Right-right. Good athlete with good actions. Timid on the bases: tiny lead, no aggressiveness at all. Stay with him.

Hal Whitaker
RHP, senior, oldest guy on the staff. Pure command-and-deception pitcher. No fastball to speak of; lives on changing speeds: knuckleball, screwball, slow breaking ball, decent curve. Fastball plays up only because everything else is so slow.

Jud Mercer
CF, senior. Can really run, and runs the bases smart. Good defender in center, arm is enough. Just isn't hitting, looks overmatched at the plate right now. Some questions about off-field habits; had a talk with him.

Chase Templeton
RHP, sophomore, big and tall. Had a stiff arm action earlier in the fall (barely bent the elbow), looked much freer this outing over three innings. Curveball fairly effective, not a plus pitch. Fastball is straight and ordinary. Threw several changeups, all off the fastball.

Harry Kowalski
RHP, sophomore. Hard thrower without a consistent arm slot: drops down and comes over the top on different pitches. Command is better when he stays directly over the top, so keep him there. Falls in love with the fastball in relief; make him throw the curveball a lot more in his next outing.

Cliff Arnaud
LHP, senior, 22, tall, fourth year in the program. Good fastball, good curveball. No idea where it's going; strike zone is wherever the catcher can reach. Doesn't come across as the sharpest kid. If the command ever shows up he's a real pitcher; stuff is good enough to earn a fall invite.

Donnie Graff
RHP, junior. Has one of the best changeups around, especially off the fastball, and he won't throw it: three all game while they hit the fastball for eight runs and nine hits over seven innings. Never shook off the catcher once. Needs to take charge of his own pitch calling.
